title: Assessment of Band Splitting Type II Radio Bursts Observed by CALLISTO Spectrometers

summary.content_summary: This study presents a detailed investigation of band splitting type II radio bursts and their association with CMEs, solar flares, and sunspot number during solar cycle 24. The primary observational data are obtained from CALLISTO spectrometers deployed at several ground stations in the e‐CALLISTO network, covering the period 2010–2017. Complementary observations from instruments such as the Hiraiso Radio Spectrograph, SOHO/LASCO coronagraph, GOES X‐ray sensors, and AIA imaging are used to provide additional context, validate CME speeds, determine solar flare peak times, and identify eruption timings. The analysis includes extraction of spectral properties from the radio dynamic spectra and correlates these with the observational records from the supporting instruments.

detectors.supporting_quote: Map showing ground stations within the e-CALLISTO network that detected the band splitting type II radio bursts: Greenland station is located at Kangerlussuaq, Greenland, and operates at 10-105 MHz. DARO is located at Hamminkeln, Germany, and works in 20-80 MHz. GAURI and OOTY are stationed at Gauribidanur and Ooty, Tamil Nadu, India, working between 45-410 MHz and 45-445 MHz, respectively. BLENSW station is in Bleien, Switzerland, and functions at 150-870 MHz. The BIR station is located at Birr Castle, Ireland, and operates within 20-90 MHz. ROSWELL-NM spectrometer is stationed in New Mexico, USA and the working frequency range is 20-90 MHz.
